I suppose I do. Actually, my husband was just saying something about that to me. He said I went from pacing around the sewing room, just sorting the exact same fabric piles over and over again... Critical of myself? Oh... yes. Lately, it's just been awful. I just keep going over every little thing. Like the bake sale last month... I keep thinking about every late order, every sharp thing I said to the volunteers. I just keep telling myself I let the church down, the historical society, this whole town, really.

Well, at home... I mean, I try to focus on the house, on my husband, but I just... I can't seem to separate it. It always comes back to the same thing. I know we've talked about it, but I just keep going over every single late order from that bake sale. Every sharp, awful thing I said to the volunteers... I made my special cranberry sauce, the one with the orange zest, and I don't even think he tasted it. It's a shame, really, people don't appreciate a good home-cooked meal anymore.

Well, yes, I suppose I am having trouble. Like I was saying, I just stopped keeping my commitments. I couldn't face the people waiting on me, so my husband has had to take over all the household routines. He even deals with the historical society for me now.

Well, yes... I suppose that's true, too. I used to love checking my garden every morning, and I was always working on my own quilt entries for the county fair. But lately... I just look at the fabric and the seed catalogs and I feel nothing much at all. It's just empty.

Well, yes, my sleep has been all over the place. For a while there, I was only sleeping a few hours a night, but I'd wake up just buzzing, ready to sew or make phone calls at three in the morning. I even called my sister in Ohio once before the sun was up. She was terrified, thought someone had died. We haven't been as close since she moved out there. Ohio is so flat, isn't it? Well, it feels like forever, to be honest. Since the orders for the quilt show fell behind and all those awful conflicts with the volunteers blew up... I've been stuck in this terrible, low, guilty place for about nine months now. Nine months. That's how long it takes to have a baby, isn't it? He was cursing a blue streak, and the dog got so scared she hid under the sofa for three hours. She's a rescue, part beagle, part goodness-knows-what, but she's got the sweetest eyes. \n\nOh dear... I've wandered off again. What were we talking about? Being critical? Yes... I just feel so guilty about everything lately, like I ruin everything I touch.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel like your guilt over things like the quilts and the bake sale is disproportionate to what actually happened?\n\nPatient: Disproportionate? Well... I don't know if it's disproportionate. It feels very real to me. I just... I keep going over every late order in my head, and every sharp thing I said to the volunteers. I just keep telling myself I let the church down, the historical society, and honestly, this whole town. \n\nThe town really relies on that bake sale, you know. We use the funds to keep the old library roof from leaking. It's a slate roof, original to the building from 1894. You can't just get anyone to fix a slate roof these days, you have to find a specialist. We had a fellow come down from Portland a few years ago to look at it, and he charged us an arm and a leg just for the estimate. Portland is getting so expensive, though. My niece lives up there, she rents a tiny little apartment that costs more than our mortgage ever did. She works in marketing, or maybe public relations? Something with computers. She's always on her phone, even at Thanksgiving dinner. It drives my husband crazy, he thinks it's so disrespectful. He actually instituted a \"no phones at the table\" rule last year, which meant we actually had to talk to each other. We ended up having a lovely conversation about... oh, what was it? Bird watching, I think. We had a pair of cardinals nesting in the lilac bush...\n\nOh, I'm so sorry. I'm rambling again, aren't I? But yes, the guilt... I just feel like I've let everyone down so terribly.\n\nDoctor: Do you often feel guilty about things beyond just the historical society project and the bake sale?\n\nPatient: Beyond just those two things? Oh, well... yes, I suppose I do. It just feels like everything I touch lately turns out wrong. I just keep going over every single late order from that bake sale, and every sharp thing I said to the poor volunteers who were just trying to help. I just keep telling myself I let the church down, the historical society, and really, this whole town. \n\nThe town isn't what it used to be, though. The downtown area used to be so bustling on a Saturday morning. You couldn't find a parking spot on Main Street if your life depended on it. Now half the storefronts are empty. They opened up that big shopping center out on Route 9, and it just pulled everyone away. My husband says it's progress, but I don't see what's progressive about a giant concrete parking lot. We used to have a lovely little hardware store right on the corner, run by Mr. Henderson. He always had a jar of butterscotch candies on the counter for the kids. My son used to love those. He's grown now, of course, living out in Denver. He sent us a picture of the snow they got last week, it was up to his knees! I don't know how people live in that kind of cold, my joints would just seize right up. I have enough trouble with my knees when it rains here...\n\nOh dear, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I just feel like I've failed everyone.\n\nDoctor: Do you ever feel an overwhelming urge to repeat certain actions or behaviors?\n\nPatient: Repeat things? Like doing something over and over? No... no, I don't think I experience anything like that. Not like my old neighbor, Mrs. Higgins. She used to sweep her front walk three times a day, regular as clockwork. She had this beautiful brick pathway leading up to her house, the old-fashioned kind with the herringbone pattern. You don't see craftsmanship like that much anymore. Everyone just pours concrete now. \n\nMy husband wanted to pour a concrete patio in our backyard last spring, but I told him it would completely ruin the look of the garden. We have these gorgeous hydrangeas back there. The soil here is so acidic, they turn the most brilliant shade of blue. I tried cutting some to bring inside last week, but I couldn't find my good pruning shears. I think my husband borrowed them to open a package and never put them back. He's always doing that with my gardening tools, just taking them and leaving them in the garage. The garage is an absolute disaster area, honestly. You can barely fit the car in there with all the boxes of old vinyl records he refuses to part with. He insists they're going to be worth money someday, but who even owns a record player anymore? Just the guilt, really.\n\nDoctor: Do you often feel guilty about things that have nothing to do with the historical society or your relationships with others?\n\nPatient: Other things? Well, I try to think about other things, but my mind just gets stuck on the same loop. I know I keep bringing it up, and I know you just asked about other things, but it's just consuming me. I just keep going over every late order in my head, and every sharp thing I said to the volunteers. I just can't stop telling myself that I let the church down, the historical society, and honestly, this whole town. \n\nEspecially how I spoke to Susan during the rush. The old signs were a lovely navy blue, very dignified. My father always said you should only trust a bank with blue signage. He was a very particular man, my father. He wore a suit and tie every single day, even on Sundays just to sit in his armchair and read the paper. You really don't see men dressing like that anymore, do you? But to answer your question, no, it always comes back to the same thing. Just that terrible feeling that I've let the church and the town down. It just won't stop playing in my head.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel guilty about things that happen in your daily life at home, not just related to the historical society or volunteer work?\n\nPatient: Well, at home... They just look everything up on those little screens. My nephew was over last Thanksgiving, and he didn't look up from his phone the entire meal. But yes, even at home, the guilt is just... it's always there, about the volunteers and the church. I just can't shake it.\n\nDoctor: Do you feel like your guilt is affecting your relationships with your family?\n\nPatient: Well, my husband... yes, it's really taken a toll on him. He's had to take over basically all the household routines, the cooking, the cleaning. I just stopped keeping any of my commitments. I couldn't even face going down to the historical society anymore, so he's been dealing with them, too. I just couldn't face the people waiting on me, knowing how badly I failed them. \n\nHe's been so patient, though.
